item.title: Nearly 90,000 told to evacuate as wildfire approaches Reno, Nevada
item.description:
An additional 45,000 people have been placed under evacuation warnings in the northwestern US state of Nevada. This comes as the fast moving Hawk fire threatens the city of Reno. According to officials the fire was "human caused", but they have not detailed if it was set intentionally. Eight hundred firefighters have been mobilized to bring the blazes under control. Unpredictable winds have complicated the effort, and so far there's been zero percent containment.

Sources: BBC News, France 24, Los Angeles Times, The Guardian

item.title: Guinea rubbish landfill collapse kills 31
item.description:
Dump site in Conakry, which minister had just promised to move, collapsed after heavy rain in west African state A ⁠landslide at a huge waste dump in Guinea’s capital has killed 30 people, the government said on Sunday, after heavy rains overnight prompted it to ⁠collapse, engulfing nearby tents and shacks. The incident occurred less than a week after the government announced plans to close the ⁠site and relocate the waste because of the threat it posed, especially during the rainy season, which causes landslides and fatal flash ⁠floods each year in crowded, underdeveloped cities across parts of West Africa. item.title: ‘No more!!!’: Trump lashes out after US-Canada talks devolve into trade war
item.description:
On this day in 2023, Donald Trump had his mugshot taken after surrendering in Fulton County, Georgia, on charges arising from his attempt to overturn the 2020 election. Trump monetized the mugshot. The case eventually collapsed. We made it to Monday! It’s Swin again. If you’re living in the U.S., you woke up this morning to our nation very much at war. No, I’m not talking about that war . Or that one . Or that other one . Or this war … Nope, not that one , either. I’m referring to the other insanely stupid war that President Donald Trump is forcing his fellow Americans to go along with – the one he’s waging on our neighbors to the north. In today’s ’ First Draft ,’ we’ll get right to the point about Trump’s latest endless war; just because the bombs aren’t falling in this one (yet?) does not make the damage any less substantial or consequential. Plus, Hakeem Jeffries takes more fire…

Covered by 1 worker-owned, 2 nonprofit, 1 public.
Sources: BBC News, The Guardian, Zeteo

item.title: Europe ramps up support to Ukraine as its US-dependent air defence runs low
item.description:
European leaders are meeting Kyiv as Ukraine holds celebrations for its 35th Independence Day. The so-called Coalition of the Willing is set to hold talks regarding support to the country, four-and-a-half years after the Russian invasion started, with the European Union having announced it was releasing over six billion euros in aid. But US support to Kyiv regarding critical air defence is still missing. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

Covered by 3 public.
Sources: Al Jazeera English, Deutsche Welle, France 24

item.title: Fast-fashion giant Shein sets cut-price $27bn valuation for Hong Kong IPO
item.description:
China-based retailer swung to $99m loss in first quarter and faces scrutiny over its environmental footprint Business live – latest updates Shein, which built a fast-fashion empire on what seemed like impossibly low prices , has been forced to lower its own valuation in a cut-price stock market float, after falling into the red earlier this year. The online retailer will list on the Hong Kong stock exchange on 1 September at a valuation of close to $27bn (£19.8bn), significantly down from a near-$100bn private market peak four years ago. item.title: Ceferin won’t challenge Infantino for FIFA presidency but tells him to quit
item.description:
Aleksander Ceferin, president of the European soccer confederation (UEFA) has announced that he will not run against Gianni Infantino but warned the under-fire FIFA president that he must either quit or face a leadership challenge in March. Infantino has been mired in a crisis since the failure of his controversial – and ultimately abandoned – plan to open FIFA to private investors.

Covered by 2 public.
Sources: Al Jazeera English, France 24

item.title: Gauff, Fils win Cincinnati tennis titles in run-up to US Open
item.description:
American beats compatriot Jessica Pegula 6-2, 6-4 Gauff claims first title of season, second in Cincinnati One year ago, Coco Gauff departed the Cincinnati Open with her career at a crossroads. On serve, she had capitulated, offering up countless double faults in most matches, and she had lost confidence in her progress and game. She believed she had to make drastic changes to her team before it was too late. It has taken an enormous amount of resilience, patience and toil, but this week Gauff began to feel the consequences of those efforts as she closed out one of the smoothest tournaments of her career with her best performance of the season, thoroughly outplaying the third seed Jessica Pegula to win 6-2, 6-4 and clinch the Cincinnati Open title for the second time in her career.
